Dear prospective learners,
It is with immense pride and a deep sense of responsibility that I welcome you to Morigaon College
(Autonomous). Having achieved autonomous status, our institution has reached a pivotal milestone in its
glorious march toward academic excellence. This prospectus serves as a testament to our commitment to
bearing the torch of knowledge for knowledge seekers.
As we move into the 2026-27 academic session, we are fully immersed in the transformative era of the
National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. Our Four-Year Undergraduate Programme (FYUGP) is
meticulously designed to provide a multidisciplinary curriculum, fostering critical thinking and innovation.
With features like the Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) and Multiple Entry-Exit Systems, we offer a
flexible, student-centric learning environment that aligns with global standards while staying rooted in our
core values.
Morigaon College is proud to introduce postgraduate programmes in Assamese, English, Political Science,
and Commerce from the academic session 2026–27, marking a significant step in expanding our academic
horizons. Alongside, the College is also launching a Postgraduate Diploma in Computer Applications
(PGDCA) to equip students with essential digital and professional skills. These initiatives reaffirm our
commitment to providing quality higher education and fostering all-inclusive development.
At Morigaon College, we believe in holistic development. Beyond our highly equipped laboratories and
well-stocked libraries, our highly efficient faculty members work tirelessly to bridge the gap between
academic rigor and real-world application. We strive to nurture not just successful professionals, but
compassionate leaders and lifelong learners.
I welcome all the aspirants to come forward and discover their capacities and potential in this temple of
learning. Join us as we embark on this exciting journey of growth and discovery.
With warm regards,




Dr. Lila Kanta Barthakur

 1. INTRODUCTION

MORIGAON COLLEGE
        Morigaon College, established on 1, July, 1964, is the oldest institution of higher
education in Morigaon district, Assam. It has witnessed 60 years of perseverance, academic
excellence and growth as one of the premier institutions nurturing and disseminating higher
education in the region.

         The college is located in the eastern part of the Morigaon town— headquarters of
Morigaon district. It is 70 kms away from Dispur, the state capital of Assam. The nearest railway
station is Jagiroad (23kms) and nearest airport is LGBI airport, Borjhar, Guwahati (96 kms).

        Since its inception, the college imparted education in the Arts stream for the first two
decades. Science stream was introduced in 1985 for facilitating a congenial environment
towards pursuing higher education in science and cultivating scientific temperament. In 2002
the college introduced several vocational and job-oriented courses like Computer Applications,
Industrial Fish and Fisheries and Functional Hindi. In 2012, Commerce Stream at degree level
was introduced to fulfill the need of higher education in Commerce for its aspirants. This fulfilled
the long felt absence of an academic centre for higher education in Commerce in the whole
region. Career-oriented courses like Functional English, Translation and Proficiency and
Entrepreneurship in Small Scale Industries were started in the academic session 2004-05.

          The college earned the pride of introducing Postgraduate Programme in Geography in
2017 and Zoology in 2018. At the U.G. level, Sociology (General Course) was introduced in the
same year. Post graduate programme in Assamese, English, Political Science and Commerce is being
introduced from 2026 along with postgraduate diploma course in Computer Application. The Chemistry
Laboratory of Morigaon College was recognized by Gauhati University as highly capable of
facilitating advanced research works. Besides, in 2020, the college introduced Bachelor of
Computer Applications and Food Processing (Agri).

        In the face of the current socio-economic scenario, the UGC has reoriented and
reshaped its policies and programmes to make the Indian higher education system career-
oriented with a focus on quality and excellence. It is in keeping with the spirit of UGC that
Morigaon College under the directives of the Government of Assam has implemented NEP
2020 from the academic session 2023-24. The professionally qualified graduates with solid
knowledge on the core disciplines and enterprises are expected to have better chances for
recruitment in service, industry, self-employment and allied sectors.

 4. Controller of Examination Office

and transparent conduct of all examination-related activities in the institution. It is responsible for
planning and organizing internal and external examinations in accordance with the guidelines of

papers securely. The office also oversees the evaluation process, compilation and timely publication
of results, and maintenance of students’ academic records. In addition, it addresses examination-
related grievances and ensures that the entire assessment system is conducted with fairness, accuracy,
and integrity.

 5. Infrastructure for Administration, Academics and Research
          The College has two administrative blocks; fourteen (14) well structured buildings with ramp
facilities; sixty two (62) well ventilated classrooms; thirty two (32) ICT enabled classrooms; four (04)
Conference cum Seminar Halls , namely, Akhil Kumar Gohain Conference Hall (AKG), Pradip
Kumar Saikia Conference Hall (PKS), Dr. Himangsu Sarmah Memorial Conference Hall (HSM), and
New Conference Hall (NCH); seventeen (17) laboratories; a research laboratory; a language
laboratory; and four (04) computer laboratories for conducting classes, organizing
seminars/conferences/workshops and carrying out research works. Additionally there is an Open
Classroom for conducting extramural classes.

         There are two (02) offices of the Principal in separate buildings in the campus; an office each,
of the Vice-Principal, the Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC), the Examination Control
Committee, and Krishna Kanta Handique State Open University (KKHSOU) — Morigaon College
Study Centre. There is a Teachers’ Common Room and nineteen (19) departmental common rooms
for the faculty of the college. There are separate office rooms for NCC, NSS, and Morigaon College
Students’ Union (MCSU). There are five (05) gates for entries and exits at different spots in the
campus.

        New Campus: 70 bighas of land at Kasomari Kishan, adjacent to the Morigaon Polytechnique
College campus has been allotted to Morigaon College in 2025.

6. Library and Reading facilities
Gurucharan Medhi Library:

The Central library, namely, Gurucharan Medhi Library is named after the founder Principal
of the College. It is an RFID based fully automated library using SOUL 3.0 software. The
library has a total collection of 44,320 books including text books and references; 18
Journals/Magazines and 8 Newspapers. Additionally, the library provides access to 6000 e-
journals and 1, 99,500 e-books under N-LIST subscription.

There is a separate ‘E-Resource cum Internet Browsing Section’ for use of students.

Book Bank facility is offered to the needy students.

Reprography facility is available at a nominal price.

Departmental Library:

In addition to the Central Library, every department has its separate library facility for
reading and borrowing of books by faculty and students.

Open Library:

There are two Open Libraries in the college aimed at encouraging and inculcating reading
habit among the students. The resources of the open libraries are made accessible to the
students without the hassles of any formal procedure. Such resources are available only for
reading purpose.

 7. Facilities for Games and Sports
Playground:

The college boasts of an expansive playground with an area of 13,560 (120x113) square
meter, with facilities for football, cricket, kho-kho, athletics, javelin throw, discus throw, high
jump, long jump, volley ball and basketball.

Indoor Stadium:

The Indoor Stadium cum Multipurpose Hall has provisions of two badminton courts, one
volleyball court, 10-meter shooting range with two Rifles and two pistols, Arm wrestling
table, table tennis boards, chess and carom boards. Yoga training sessions are conducted on
regular basis.

Gymnasium:

The gymnasium is well equipped with tread mill for cardiovascular exercises; dumb bells, bar
bells, leg press, chest press et al for strength training. The gymnasium has provisions for
weight lifting, power lifting and bodybuilding.

8. Canteen Facilities
College Canteen:

The college has a well furnished canteen with seating capacity of 80. There is a separate air
conditioned room for use of faculty and guests. The canteen caters to the standards of
cleanliness and hygiene with reasonable prices against its menu.

Cafeteria:

The cafeteria provides a quick snack to the teachers and students who have little time to spare
in between classes.

Swahid Giribala Deka Girls’ Hostel has been functioning since the year 2000. It has seat
capacity for 100 boarders.

SC Girls’ Hostel:

SC Girls’ Hostel was set up for the girls' students belonging to SC category in the year 2019
and has been functioning since. It has seat capacity of 30 boarders.

Swahid Mudra Patar Boys’ Hostel:

Swahid Mudra Patar Boys’ Hostel was set up in 1980 and has a capacity of 25 boarders.

 10. Health Care facilities
   •   Sick Room:
       There is a two bedded sickroom for use by students, teachers and staff during
       imminent conditions. It offers basic medical care, first aid and treatment for minor
       illnesses or injuries.

   •   Day Care Centre:
       The day care centre provides child care services for faculty and staff.

   •   Drinking Water Station:
       The college has four drinking water stations with water purifiers and water coolers for
       use of students. Additionally, there are 13 water purifiers in different locations within
       the campus.
       There are separate water coolers & purifiers in the hostels for use of hostel boarders.

   •   Ambulance:
       There is an Ambulance facility to meet any situation arising out of an emergency. It
       provides medical transportation and care to students, faculty and staff in moments of
       crises. This facility can also be availed by people of the community as and when
       deemed necessary by making a minimal payment to the college.

   •   First Aid Facility:
       First aid facility is available for tending to minor injuries and illnesses.

   •   Sanitary Pad Vending Machines:
       There are two sanitary pad vending machines for the convenience of the girl students.
       These vending machines provide sanitary pads at a nominal rate.

   •   Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Speakers’ Corner:

12. Pro-Environment Initiatives
  •   Laboratory Waste Water Treatment Units:
      The Department of Chemistry, Morigaon College has set up three units for laboratory
      waste water treatment. As a part of its commitment to environmental sustainability
      and safe laboratory practices, these units are designed to treat chemical affluence
      generated from laboratory experiments and practical sessions, ensuring that hazardous
      substances are neutralized or removed before disposal.

  •   Air Quality Monitoring Station:
      The Air Quality Monitoring Station is set up under National Air Quality Monitoring
      Programme (NAMP) financed by the Central Pollution Control Board. Currently, the
      monitoring station is under the supervision of the Department of Chemistry in
      collaboration with Pollution Control Board, Assam. The air quality parameters under
      study are PM 10, PM 2.5, NO2 and SO2.

  •   Larvivorous Fish Tanks
      For controlling mosquito borne diseases viz. malaria, dengue in the campus, there are
      four larvivorous fish tanks for breeding of Guppy fish Gambusia affinis. These small
      freshwater fish feed on mosquito larvae making them a natural form of mosquito
      control. This is an environment friendly alternative to chemical pesticides.

  •   Rain Water Harvesting:
      There are two tanks for harvesting of rain water, which is later used for non potable
      purposes in the campus.

  •   Green House:
      The Green House was set up in the year 2007-08 by Anti Global Warming Society,
      Morigaon – a local NGO. It is a noble step towards protecting the degrading
      environmental conditions. It aims at motivating the students and the local populace in
      creating environmental awareness.

  •   Campus Pond:
      It is a step towards conservation of local bio-diversity by creating a natural habitat for
      supporting birds, fishes and other aquatic species.




                                                                                              8
   •   Campus Bio-diversity Register:
      It is a comprehensive data base that documents and tracks the various plant and
      animal species found on campus. It is attempted at encouraging student involvement
      in bio-diversity conservation and research.
      For encouraging awareness among the students, the trees in the campus are provided
      with QR codes, disclosing valuable information pertaining to their medicinal and
      commercial uses.

  •   Solar Panels
      The solar panels are used in the campus as a sustainable source of power for building
      and lighting.

13. Self Sustenance Measures and Skill Development Initiatives
  •   Live stock Rearing:
      Dairy farming and Goat farming in the campus provide an avenue for skill
      development as well as revenue generations by selling off fresh animal products. It
      gives an opportunity to the students to learn about economic sustainability through
      animal husbandry.

  •   Vermicompost Unit:
      The initiative of producing vermicompost enables sustainable agricultural practices in
      the campus. This unit is jointly maintained by the Departments of Chemistry and
      Botany. The bio-fertiliser produced by this unit is packaged and marketed.

  •   Horticulture Farm:
      The horticulture farm covering an area of 0.311 acres grows jujube, lemons, banana,
      litchi, mango, dragon fruit, guava, through organic farming and aids in revenue
      generation.

  •   Duckery:
      The Duckery was started as a part of the ‘Earn when you Learn’ initiative of the
      Department of Zoology. This has been functioning since 2021, aimed at giving ten
      ducklings each to the economically challenged students for learning the rearing
      process and receiving economic benefits.

  •   Cutting and Tailoring Centre:
      This centre is committed at making the students economically self sufficient by
      providing hands on training and practical experience in designing, cutting and sewing
      garments using various fabrics and techniques.

15. Infrastructure and Facilities for Recreation
       Boys’ Common Room:
       The Boys’ Common Room is designed for relaxation and recreation of the students
       with seating arrangements and a recreational corner.

       Girls’ Common Rooms:
       There are two Girls’ Common Rooms in the college for use of the girl students. These
       rooms are well furnished with furniture, washrooms and drinking water facilities.
       There is a recreational corner in each of the common room with provisions for indoor
       games viz. carom, ludo and chess.

       Teachers’ Common Room:
       The Teachers’ Common Room is a space designed adequately for providing the
       faculty members for engaging in discussions in matters related to the academic and
       administrative affairs of the college. Located conveniently within the main building,
       the room is furnished with comfortable seating and basic amenities like LCD
       television, water purifier, fans and newspapers. This is a much a coveted common
       space for holding discussions with teachers across disciplines.

       Departmental Common Rooms for Faculty:
       Each department in the college has its own Departmental Common Room where the
       teachers of the respective department can prepare for the classes, hold academic
       discussions and departmental meetings. These are well equipped with furniture,
       computers, printers, internet and other facilities necessary for smooth running of the
       department.

16. Institution-Community Linkages

       NCC:
       The National Cadet Corps (NCC) Unit, Morigaon College is an integral part of the
       institution’s commitment to fostering discipline, leadership and national and
       community service among its students. Affiliated with the 8th Assam Battalion, NCC,


                                                                                          10
       Nagaon, under the Directorate of NCC, Shillong, the unit is open to both male and
      female cadets.

      NSS:
      The National Service Scheme (NSS) Unit, of Morigaon College plays a pivotal role in
      fostering community engagement and social responsibility among the students.
      Notably, the NSS unit has conducted flood relief camps, providing essential aid to the
      affected communities; cleanliness drives under “Swacchta hi Sewa” programme,
      thereby instilling a sense of civic duty and volunteerism among the students of the
      college.

      Adopted Villages:
      As a part of its commitment to community outreach and social responsibility, the
      College has adopted eight villages under the “Unnat Bharat Abhiyan” (UBA), a
      flagship programme of the Ministry of Education, Govt. of India, aimed at connecting
      Institutions of Higher Education with local communities to address developmental
      challenges. The adopted villages namely are, Oujaribori, Solmari Mikir Gaon, Bori
      Gaon, Mayanguri, Bhoiraguri, Gerakhowa, Moidhali Pothar and Tengaguri. The
      college conducts health camps, sanitation drives, educational outreach, environmental
      awareness programmes and provides socio-economic services. The college has a
      provision of seat reservation in each Stream for the meritorious students of the
      adopted villages.

17. Organisations within the Campus
  •   Morigaon College Teachers’ Unit:
      Morigaon College Teachers’ Unit is affiliated to Assam College Teachers’
      Association and concerns itself with the interest of the teachers and their holistic
      academic and professional experience. It promotes academic activities and plays a
      vital role in the overall development of the College.

  •   Morigaon Mahavidyalaya Mahila Mancha:
      The Women’s Forum of the College, Morigaon Mahavidyalaya Mahila Mancha
      (MMMM) was established on 29th November, 2005 to providing a common platform
      for the female staff of the college for raising their concerns and safeguarding their
      interests. The Mancha is also committed to community welfare programmes viz.
      sensitizing the rural women on their socio-economic rights; providing them support in
      areas of health and hygiene and raising awareness against social evils.

  •   Morigaon College Employees’ Unit:
      This unit was formed to promote and look after the needs and interests of the College

                     Department of ITEP (Middle Stage)
With the commencement of the ITEP Department in August, 2026 a new pathway opens for
aspiring educators to grow as thoughtful and compassionate facilitators of learning. The
Middle Stage, focusing on Grades 6 to 8, recognizes adolescence as a sensitive and
meaningful phase where learners seek identity, confidence, and connection.
This stage is guided by a humanistic pattern that values each learner as a whole person—
thinking, feeling, and evolving. Future teachers are encouraged to create classrooms where
respect, empathy, and openness form the foundation of learning. Education here is not limited
to textbooks; it becomes a shared journey of discovery, dialogue, and understanding.

The programme blends subject learning with real-life experiences, helping trainees connect
knowledge with the lived realities of students. Through school exposure, reflective practices,
and interactive teaching, they learn to listen, guide, and support rather than simply instruct.
Attention is given to emotional well-being, inclusivity, and nurturing a sense of belonging
among all learners.

As the department begins in August, it carries a vision of shaping educators who inspire trust,
encourage curiosity, and help young adolescents grow into confident, responsible, and
empathetic individuals.
